passages.original: Quod gratia Dei praestet ut lex impleatur, non, sicut ait Pelagius, facile quasi sine gratia Dei difficilia possint impleri. Conc. eod. tit. 5.
passages.english: That the grace of God grants that the law be fulfilled, [and] not, as Pelagius says, [merely] that difficult things may be fulfilled easily, as if they could [be fulfilled] without the grace of God. Council, same, title 5.
passages.notes: Chapter heading from a canonical collection. The Latin is compressed: Pelagius' view is that grace only makes easier what could be done, with difficulty, without it. The source reference 'Conc. eod.' (same council) refers to a council named in an earlier heading not given here, probably the Council of Carthage of 418.

passages.original: Quod gratia Dei non solum peccata dimittat, sed etiam adjuvet ne committantur, et praestet ut lex impleatur, non, sicut ait Pelagius, facile quasi sine Dei gratia difficilius possit impleri. Epist. ead. tit. 10.
passages.english: That the grace of God not only forgives sins but also helps [us] not to commit them, and grants that the law be fulfilled, [and] not, as Pelagius says, [merely] that it may be fulfilled easily, as if it could be fulfilled with more difficulty without the grace of God. Letter, same, title 10.
passages.notes: 'difficilius' (more difficultly) differs from 'difficilia' in the parallel heading; the sense is the same Pelagian position, that without grace the law can be fulfilled, only with greater difficulty. 'Epist. ead.' (same letter) refers to a letter named in an earlier heading not given here.
